name: Turi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Peterson, Minz, Linda & Khan (2024), Turi chapter in The Munda Languages (2nd ed., Routledge) - cited for Turi phonology in Wikipedia; full text not reachable

sources.citation: Peterson, John; Minz, Abhay Sagar; Linda, Prabhat; Khan, Ariba; Kachhap, Francis Xavier; Gari, Manish (2024). "A Brief Introduction to the Turi Language of Eastern India". Bhasha 3(2): 261-302. DOI 10.30687/bhasha/2785-5953/2024/02/005 (open access, CC BY 4.0).
sources.note: Section 2.1 Phonology (pp. 266-267) gives only consonant and vowel inventories (notes vowel length is not phonemic); nothing on stress placement. The only accent remark is p. 283: 'as no studies have yet been carried out on lexical accent in Turi or how this is to be defined, all primary and secondary accents were removed from the data for all varieties before comparison.' Appendix 1 word list carries no stress marks.

sources.citation: Osada, Toshiki (1991). "Father Ponette's Field Note on Turi with a Comparative Vocabulary". Journal of Asian and African Studies (ILCAA, Tokyo) 42: 175-189. hdl:10108/21782.
sources.note: Wordlist (IPA, unaccented) from Ponette's 1950s-80s field notes with Santali/Mundari/Ho/Sadri comparanda; no statement on stress or accent. Intro: 'Studies of the Turi language are very few.. That is all that is on record for Turi' (p. 175).

sources.citation: Konow, Sten (1906). "Tūrī". In Grierson, G. A. (ed.), Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IV: Muṇḍā and Dravidian Languages, pp. 128-134. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. (Glottolog ref 96384, listed by Glottolog as a minimal description)
sources.note: Two-page note plus three specimens; states the dialect's phonology 'agrees with Santali in most points' and gives a few sound correspondences; nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: John Peterson, staff page, ISFAS Kiel (publications on Turi).
sources.note: Lists only the 2024 Bhasha article, Peterson & Minz (2021) My First Turi Picture Book (primer, Ranchi), and 2020-2022 talks/workshop on Turi documentation; no grammar or phonology.
Consonant/vowel notes only, all drawn from Peterson et al. 2024; no stress information.

sources.citation: Anderson, Gregory D. S; Osada, Toshiki; Harrison, K. David (2008). "Ho and the other Kherwarian languages". In G. D. S. Anderson (ed.), The Munda Languages, 195-255. London/New York: Routledge.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher
sources.note: The only Kherwarian survey chapter that might contain a Turi paragraph or a general Kherwarian stress statement; not opened (Routledge, paywalled). Low likelihood of a Turi-specific stress rule.

sources.citation: Peterson, John & Abhay Sagar Minz et al., Kiel/Ranchi Turi documentation project (2020-), corpus and any forthcoming Turi grammar or phonology.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Peterson et al. 2024 state lexical accent is unstudied; any future fuller grammar or instrumental study from this project would be the first-hand source for Turi stress.

sources.citation: Munda, Ram Dayal (1968). Proto-Kherwarian Phonemic System. Unpublished MA thesis, University of Chicago.

sources.note: Cited by Osada 1991 and Peterson et al. 2024 as the only other work placing Turi within Kherwarian; may contain remarks on Kherwarian accent. Unpublished thesis, library only.

sources.citation: Anderson, Gregory D. S. (ed.) (2008). The Munda Languages. London/New York: Routledge (Routledge product page TOC).
